newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Strong debut seen for Changan on Friday.
newsitem.headline: Strong debut seen for Changan on Friday.

text.p: Chongqing Changan Automobile Co Ltd is expected to make an impressive debut when its 250 million B shares start trading in Shenzhen on Friday, analysts said.
They said Changan's good earnings record, foreign institutional interest in China's car industry and the good outlook for market as a whole all augured well for the company.

A broker at a major Chinese brokerage told the China Securities Bulletin, a Hong Kong-based newsletter, that Changan's listing debut would be supported by Suzuki Motor Corp having bought a considerable stake at a higher price.

Suzuki, its affiliate American Suzuki Motor Corp and Nissho Iwai Corp own 50 percent of Changan's B shares, bought at a price equivalent to 2.96 yuan per share, and have pledged to retain their shares for at least three years.
The other 125 million B shares were offered to overseas investors at HK$1.89 each, Changan said in its B share listing notice.
Changan was likely to close its first trading day above HK$2.00, said a broker at China Southern Securities.
"Compared with Jiangling Motors, Changan's earnings record is much stronger, so Changan's price level must be higher than Jiangling," the broker said.
Jiangling B shares closed at HK$1.95 per share on Wednesday. Shortly before the close on Thursday they were trading at HK$2.00.
Another broker said potential local demand for small cars, Changan's core product, was very strong and Changan's B shares would yield attractive long-term returns.
Changan could test the HK$2.10 level over the short term, he added.

A broker at an overseas brokerage's unit in Shenzhen said some overseas institutions had failed to subscribe for Changan's B shares and their buying in the secondary market would support its share price.
He said Changan's share offer was about six times subscribed, which reflected overseas investor interest. He added he expected Changan to gain about 10 percent on its debut.
A local analyst said that with Suzuki's help Changan's production technology could be upgraded and competitiveness improved. Buying Changan below HK$2.00 caried little risk, he said.

China has seven major small car makers, who together produced 347,060 vehicles last year, accounting for 87.83 percent of national output, according to Shanghai Guotai Securities, Changan's listing promoter.
Changan ranked first with an output of 70,618 units, the brokerage said said in a report in Thursday's Shenzhen-based Securities Times.
The seven sold a combined 345,394 units last year, of which Changan accounted for 66,178, Guotai said.

Changan, based in the city of Chongqing in southwestern Sichuan province, said in a prospectus that it would use proceeds from the offer to expand its automobile output and upgrade production facilities and technology.
Based on international accounting standards Changan forecast net earnings of at least 220 million yuan this year, compared with 220.16 million in 1995 and 192.52 million in 1994.
Changan said it had after-tax profits of 82.63 million yuan in the first half of this year.
